sections.head: Anaheim welcomed 26.5 million visitors who spent $6.83 billion in 2025
sections.dek: Tourism Economics forecasts 27.0 million visitors and $7.2 billion for 2026; the OC Vibe area already accounts for 5.2% of Anaheim visitor days.
sections.ans: In 2025, 26.5M visitors spent $6.83B in Anaheim, $258 each ($6.832B ÷ 26.5M), and supported 67,817 jobs (Tourism Economics, published 2026). Tourism Economics forecasts 27.0M visitors (+1.9%) and $7.2B (+5.6%) for 2026. These are City of Anaheim totals; they do not measure OC Vibe. For the OC Vibe area today, Datafy measured 5.2% of Anaheim visitor days in 2024, and 85.8% of District 5 visitors stay overnight (Azira, Jan.–May 2026).

sections.q: How many visitors come to Orange County, from where and when, who are they, and what hotel capacity serves them?
sections.period: CIC Research 2009-2019; Tourism Economics 2021-2025; CoStar through Sept. 2026; Azira Jan. 2023-Aug. 2026
sections.ans: Orange County drew 51.3M visitors in 2025, 29.2M for the day and 22.1M overnight, and 93.3% came from within the U.S. (Tourism Economics). Most come for leisure: in 2019, 81.2% traveled for pleasure or to see friends and relatives, in parties of 2.8, and 37.0% brought children (CIC Research). Hotels filled 75.2% of 60,224 rooms at $221.67 in Jan.-Aug. 2026, with July the busiest month (CoStar).

notes: The five questions, as sent by Entertainment + Culture Advisors on Oct. 19, 2026: (1) How many visitors came to Orange County each year from 2019 to 2025, and so far in 2026, split by domestic and international and by overnight and day? (2) Where do visitors come from, and can the Los Angeles-Long Beach-Anaheim area be split into Anaheim and outside Anaheim? (3) How does visitation change month by month? (4) What is the purpose of the trip, how long do visitors stay, how large is the travel party and how many travel with children? (5) How many hotel rooms does Orange County have, and what are occupancy and average daily rate?

Two visitor series exist and are kept apart: CIC Research for Visit Anaheim (2009-2019, survey-based) and Tourism Economics (2021-2025, model-based). CIC counted 50.21M visitors in 2019; Tourism Economics counted 51.3M in 2025. Neither publishes 2020 for the county; Dean Runyan Associates shows county visitor spending fell to 46.7% of its 2019 level that year.

Origins can be shown at the metro-area level. The Los Angeles-Long Beach-Anaheim metro area includes all of Orange County, and Azira does not supply ZIP codes, so a split between Anaheim and the rest of the metro area is not available from current sources.
Monthly visitor counts are not published for Orange County. Hotel occupancy is the monthly measure: July averaged 80.6% and January 61.2% over 2023-2025 (CoStar).
The most recent Orange County visitor profile is CIC Research's 2019 study; no newer county survey was found in Visit Anaheim's SharePoint or in Visit California's research (searched Oct. 19, 2026).
ocv: OC Vibe opens into a county of 51.3M visitors, 22.1M of them overnight (2025).
Family travel is a core audience: 37.0% of county visitors and 42.0% of Anaheim visitors traveled with children in 2019.
Special events already draw 7.6% of county visitors and 10.5% of day visitors (2019), a base for arena and concert programming.

Hotel rooms are tightest in July (80.6%) and June (76.4%) and most open in January (61.2%), December (68.9%) and February (69.0%), CoStar 2023-2025 averages: event dates in the open months fill rooms that would otherwise sit empty.

ocv: OC Vibe already appears in 5.2% of Anaheim visitor days (Datafy, 2024), before the new venues open. This is the baseline to measure OC Vibe's growth against.

District 5 visitors are 85.8% overnight and 43.8% first-time, and 44% of domestic visitors come from outside California (Texas, Virginia, Florida, Arizona and New York lead). Out-of-state visitors are the ones who bring new money to California.
13.7% of District 5 visitors also go to the Anaheim Resort, so packaging OC Vibe with resort stays is a direct way to add a day.

New markets: beyond Southern California, the largest visitor spending comes from San Francisco, Seattle, Phoenix, Las Vegas, San Jose, Sacramento, Orlando, New York and Detroit, and internationally from Mexico ($5.2M), Canada and Japan (Visa, Aug. 2026). These are fly-in markets where OC Vibe events can justify a longer trip.

International visitors spent $5.4M on restaurants and dining in August 2026, but that was down 19.1% from a year earlier, while retail rose 9.3% (Visa). Dining is OC Vibe's biggest category and the one to watch with international guests.

notes: Food and beverage is a growing part of hotel revenue. Over the past 12 months, Disneyland submarket hotels earned 22.4% of revenue from food and beverage, and food revenue per available room rose 28.9%. Countywide the share is 29.4%. Labor is the largest cost: 41.8% of revenue in the Disneyland submarket.

Leisure and hospitality is a specialty of the county: 244K jobs, 1.3 times the U.S. concentration, growing +2.69% vs. +1.59% nationally. Median household income is $121,883, 43% above the U.S. CoStar describes a drive market of 20 million people within 90 miles.
Costs: California's minimum wage is $16.50 (2025), and Anaheim's resort-area living-wage ordinance brought covered Disney wages to $20.42 in 2025.
Conventions, as cited by CoStar from Visit Anaheim: 142 events secured for 2026, projected at about $1.74 billion in economic impact and nearly 600,000 hotel room nights.

Investment: hotel sales slowed with higher borrowing costs. In May 2026 a 352-room hotel at 101 E. Katella Ave. sold for $78.75 million ($223,722 per room). CoStar notes that the OC Vibe district could create opportunities for future hotel investment.
CoStar describes OC Vibe as a $4 billion project with full buildout targeted by 2028. LARC reports $5 billion with a final phase by 2033. OC Vibe's own figures should be used.
CoStar's "Disneyland" and "Anaheim" submarkets split the city's hotels. The exact boundary around OC Vibe could not be confirmed from the CoStar map.
STR hotel sets: groups filled 18.2% of rooms sold at Anaheim+ hotels in 2026 at $228 a night; leisure and other transient guests filled 80.9% at $245.

2026 hotel calendar (STR, Jan.–Sept.): weeknights had the most open rooms in Jan., May, Aug. and Sept. (64%–74% full); July had the most nights at 90%+ (10); groups took the largest share of rooms in Feb. (25.0%) and Mar. (22.2%). Use these windows to schedule events that need hotel rooms, and avoid peak nights for large out-of-town groups.
ocv: The market can absorb these rooms: resort-area hotels run 78.4% occupancy, and only 668 rooms are under construction countywide.
Each point of occupancy at OC Vibe's hotels equals about 2,000 room nights and $438,000 in room revenue at the county average rate.

Sunday and Monday are the open nights: Visit Anaheim hotels ran 70.6% occupancy on those nights in 2026 vs. 86.2% on Fridays and Saturdays (STR). Each point OC Vibe adds on Sunday and Monday nights is about 22,200 room nights and $5.1M in room revenue a year.
The rest of Anaheim (CoStar's Anaheim submarket) averages $130 a night vs. $255 in the resort area. Where OC Vibe's hotels price between those two will drive their revenue more than occupancy.

notes: Transit: Route 50 (Katella Ave) reaches the Katella/Harbor resort area from ARTIC in about 14 minutes and Route 553 in about 15. Weekend one-seat service to the resort drops to 29 trips on Saturday (Route 553 does not run). The single-ride bus fare is $2.00.

Late events: 16 weekday bus trips stop at ARTIC after 10 p.m. (11 leaving, 5 ending there); the last departure is at 1:38 a.m.. The bus data does not include Metrolink or Amtrak trains, which also serve ARTIC.

The 2026 traffic map repeats older counts near OC Vibe: freeway volumes are from 2024, and Katella Ave next to the district was last counted in 2021. New counts before OC Vibe's 2027 openings would set a clean baseline.

Cost trends (BTS): driving a car cost $0.82 per mile in 2024, up 32% from 2019; West Coast gasoline averaged $4.09 in 2025, about $1 above the U.S.; domestic airfares averaged $387 (+10% since 2019). LARC and Tourism Economics note gas prices spiked again in spring 2026, which weighs most on drive-market visitors.

County context (BTS): 67.5% of Orange County workers drive alone and 1.2% use public transportation; 4.8% of households (51,573) have no vehicle. The county has one medium-hub airport (John Wayne), 68 miles of passenger rail track and 1,181 bridges (2.8% in poor condition).

Drive market and air (CoStar): about 20 million people live within 90 miles, which makes driving the main way visitors arrive. John Wayne Airport handled a record 11.74 million passengers in 2023 and 11.09 million in 2024, on 13 commercial airlines.
Source note: the 2026 ADT file is OCTA's Traffic Flow Map, not Visit California data. Tourism Economics transportation impact data has not been received yet.
Rail data are station totals (Amtrak) and line totals (Metrolink); ARTIC station-level Metrolink boardings were not available.

Orange County transit ridership peaked at 70.7M passengers in 2007 and fell to 43.8M by 2017 (-38%), while OCTA's vehicle fleet grew from 615 to 1,066. Expenses per passenger rose from $3.28 to $7.00. For OC Vibe this means most guests will drive, and that buses have spare seats outside peak hours. Solution: pair event-night service requests with ticket-and-transit promotions so added buses fill.

Orange County transit, 2003–2017: OCTA's staff fell 14.6% (1,786 to 1,526), with the largest drop after 2009 (2,235 to 1,585), while its expenses rose 17.9% ($193.4M to $227.9M), or from $108K to $149K per employee. Specialized service expenses grew fastest ($23.0M to $75.1M, +227%). Countywide, expenses exceeded revenues in 10 of 15 years (2017: −$0.9M). A leaner, cost-pressured system can limit how much extra event-night service OCTA adds on short notice. Solution: OC Vibe should request event-night service early, share its event calendar with OCTA, and consider co-funding late-night service on its biggest nights. The data ends in 2017, so it shows the long-term trend, not today's budgets.
ocv: About 275,000 vehicles a day pass OC Vibe on SR-57, and 20 million people live within a 90-mile drive (CoStar). Most OC Vibe visitors will arrive by car, so parking (12,369–12,823 planned spaces) and event-day traffic plans matter.
ARTIC's 277 weekday bus trips and the 2028 Katella pedestrian bridge are OC Vibe's transit front door. Only 11 buses leave ARTIC after 10 p.m., which limits late-event trips without a car.
Rising travel costs (West Coast gas $4.09 a gallon in 2025; average domestic airfare $387) favor nearby drive markets, which are OC Vibe's core audience.

Travelers already treat ARTIC as a parking and transit hub for Disneyland and the convention center (29 of 53 related trip-planner messages), and ask about late returns. OC Vibe can meet that traffic with dining and evening programming at the ARTIC end of the district.

Rail already brings visitors to OC Vibe's front door: 191,153 Amtrak passengers used the Anaheim station at ARTIC in 2024 (79% of the 2018 level), mostly on trips under 100 miles from San Diego and Los Angeles. 15.6 million people live within 50 miles of the station.

Metrolink's Orange County Line carries 5,116 weekday riders and is growing (+4%), and 55% of Metrolink trips are not commutes. Weekend ridership is down, so event-night rail service is a gap to raise with Metrolink and OCTA.

notes: Demand drivers near OC Vibe: Honda Center (Anaheim Ducks and concerts), Angel Stadium, ARTIC, the Anaheim Convention Center (1.8 million sq ft) and DisneylandForward ($1.9 billion; Avengers Campus expansion opening 2027). OC Sports & Entertainment now employs about 3,000 locally (up from 2,000 in the June report).

Events: the 2028 Summer Olympics include cycling and volleyball events in Anaheim, and LARC expects a 2028 hotel lift from them. The 2026 World Cup lifted rates this year but becomes a tough comparison in Q2–Q3 2027. Solution: set 2027 targets against 2025 as well as 2026.
Office: Orange County office vacancy was 14.4% in Q2 2026 (down 3.4 points from a year earlier); Kiln took 39,000 sq ft in the Stadium Area, where The Weave adds 168,000 sq ft of Class A space.

Costs and inflation: Anaheim consumer prices are forecast to rise 3.2% a year over three years (3.3% in 2026, 3.5% in 2027), above the U.S. Hotel wages are forecast to grow 2.6% a year, about 6.0% a year in total labor cost, and LA County's $30 hotel minimum wage (by 2030) may pressure Orange County wages. Solution: build these costs into OC Vibe pricing and staffing plans, and cross-train staff across venues.

Risks LARC flags: higher gas prices and airfares tied to the Iran conflict, a possible 2026 federal shutdown, midterm-election softness in Q4 2026, and slower U.S. job growth. Solution: lean on drive markets within 90 miles, flexible packages and midweek convention groups.

takeaways: Anaheim's visitor economy: 26.5M visitors spent $6.83B in 2025 and supported 67,817 jobs; Tourism Economics forecasts 27.0M visitors and $7.2B for 2026. These are City of Anaheim totals; the OC Vibe area accounted for 5.2% of Anaheim visitor days in 2024. (Source: Tourism Economics, Economic Impact of Visitors (calendar 2025; pub. 2026); Tourism Economics, Anaheim Travel Forecast (Sept. 2026); Datafy Anaheim visitor report (calendar 2024))

Orange County market: 51.3M visitors in 2025 (22.1M overnight; 93.3% domestic); 55.4% from Southern California and 37.0% traveling with children (2019); 60,224 hotel rooms at 75.2% occupancy and $221.67 ADR in Jan.-Aug. 2026, with July the peak month. (Source: Tourism Economics, Economic Impact of Visitors to Orange County, 2025 (pub. May 2026); CIC Research, Annual Profile of Visitors to Anaheim and Orange County, 2019 (for Visit Anaheim, Apr. 2020); CoStar, Orange County hotel market (monthly data through Sept. 2026; market report Oct. 12, 2026))

Getting to OC Vibe: SR-57 beside the district carries about 275,000 vehicles a weekday; ARTIC has 277 weekday bus trips but only 11 leave after 10 p.m.; the City lists 12,369–12,823 planned parking spaces. (Source: OCTA Traffic Flow Map (pub. Aug. 2026) and bus schedules (Aug. 9–Nov. 7, 2026); City of Anaheim OCVibe page (2026); OCVIBE fact sheet (Apr. 2024))

Visitors spend more each trip: about $258 per Anaheim visitor in 2025, forecast to reach $279 by 2028; Q2 2026 spending rose 7.8%. (Calculation: $6.83B visitor spending ÷ 26.5M visitors = $258 per visitor) (Source: Tourism Economics, Economic Impact 2025 (pub. Apr.–May 2026); Tourism Economics, Travel Forecast (pub. Sept. 2026; data to Aug. 31, 2026))
The visitor economy supports 67,817 Anaheim jobs (one in three); food and beverage is 16.8% of them, 29.1% countywide. (Source: Tourism Economics, Economic Impact 2025 (pub. Apr.–May 2026))

One more night per visitor is worth about $794 million in lodging spending, and about $1.0 billion counting all spending by overnight visitors. main.head: Anaheim's visitor market is growing into OC Vibe's 2027 opening
main.dek: Visitors spent $1.76 billion in Q2 2026 (+7.8%), hotel revenue per room rose 11.4%, and Convention Center room nights for 2027 are pacing 17% ahead.
main.lede: Anaheim's visitor economy is expanding ahead of OC Vibe's first openings in early 2027, Visit Anaheim Business Intelligence reported. Visitors spent $1.76 billion in the second quarter of 2026, up 7.8% from a year earlier (Tourism Economics, Sept. 2026), and hotel revenue per available room rose 11.4% (LARC, Sept. 2026).
paras: The OC Vibe area already accounts for 5.2% of Anaheim visitor days (Datafy, 2024). In District 5, 85.8% of visitors stay overnight and 43.8% are first-time visitors (Azira, Jan.–May 2026).

Hotels have room on weeknights. Visit Anaheim's hotels ran 70.6% full on Sunday–Monday nights in 2026 vs. 86.2% on Friday–Saturday, and Jan., May, Aug. and Sept. weeknights had the most open rooms (STR, Jan.–Sept. 2026). Each point of Sunday–Monday occupancy is worth about $5.1M in room revenue a year (21,318 rooms × 1 point × 104 Sunday and Monday nights a year = 22,171 room nights; × $229.90 average Sunday–Monday rate = $5.1M).

Groups are a growing source of weekday guests. Convention Center room nights for 2027 are pacing 17% ahead (LARC, Sept. 2026), and Disney's D23 evening showcases drew 36,000+ guests to Honda Center over three nights alongside the Convention Center expo (BizBash, Sept. 2026).

Most visitors drive: 74.0% of domestic trips start within 50 miles, and SR-57 beside the district carries about 275,000 vehicles a weekday (Azira, Aug. 2026; OCTA, Aug. 2026). ARTIC adds 277 weekday bus trips, Amtrak and Metrolink, but only 11 buses leave after 10 p.m.

The full report covers Anaheim and the OC Vibe area today, visitor spending, jobs, one more night, getting here, who visits, marketing reach, hotels and the market outlook, with the source and date for every figure.
